subject: Alignment & procurement framing — NimbleHealth initial discovery
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial discovery recap + next steps (NimbleHealth)

Hi Samir — really appreciate you taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please flag any corrections.

Pain points you described:
- Production latency spikes and high token cost on nightly batch inference for clinical note summarization.
- Fragmented caching: each team runs separate models, no shared KV cache, causing waste on repeated prefixes.
- Compliance: need SOC2 evidence and tighter audit logs for downstream regulators.

Current stack (what you told us):
- On-prem primary data store; AWS for model serving (EC2 + SageMaker endpoints today)
- Mix of Llama-2-family fine-tuned models and an internal smaller reranker

Success criteria for a first phase (we captured):
1) Reduce per-token inference cost by >=30% while keeping 95th pct latency < 250ms for interactive queries.
2) Maintain/raise throughput for nightly batch jobs (same budget) and shorten batch windows by 20%.
3) Provide exportable audit logs (retention 1y) and SOC2 artifacts for procurement review.

Procurement framing / decision process (based on call):
- Primary decision owner: Maria Gomez (CPO) — commercial + product sign-off
- Technical approver: Head of infra (TBD) — will own integration and SOC/security sign-off
- Target procurement window: mid-September (internal budget cycle).
- Initial commercial guardrail: flexible month-to-month hosted trial leading to a 12–24mo reserved commitment if SLAs and cost targets are met. Rough target unit economics: <$0.002/token (for the long tail workload) — we’ll propose options.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Vivek — needs to cover KV caching options and quantization profiles (please share 60–90 min slots next week).
2) I’ll send an SOW skeleton and 3 commercial options (trial, reserved minimal, reserved + priority) for Maria + procurement to review.
3) We’ll include SOC2 checklist and a short security one-pager for Diego/infra team.

Attachments: 20260830-discovery-notes.pdf, initial-commercial-grid.xlsx (first-pass guardrails).

Would you confirm the decision makers above and the September timeline? Also, what is the best way to get Diego/infra (or whoever is owning infra) into the technical call?

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-2134

From: Samir Khan <samir.k@nimblehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial discovery recap + next steps (NimbleHealth)

Thanks Rishi — this is a great write-up and accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- Decision makers: Maria Gomez (CPO) will sign off commercially; I will coordinate with our Head of IT Security (Alicia Chen) and our Infra lead (we will name them on Monday) for the technical and SOC review.
- Timeline: mid-September is correct; procurement wants a 2–3 week evaluation window once we have pricing and SOC artifacts.
- Target: cost reduction and latency improvement are the priority for product teams; procurement cares about term flexibility and SLAs.

We’re good to schedule the technical session. Vivek — do you have availability Tuesday/Wed next week (Sep 1–2) afternoons PT?

I’ll loop Maria and Alicia after I confirm their calendars. Also please include any redlines or contract caveats we should expect for an initial trial (data residency, ingress/egress, audit support).

Samir Khan
Director of Product Operations, NimbleHealth
samir.k@nimblehealth.com
